chunks.text: In 1726, an English woman convinced some of the top doctors in the country that she was giving birth to rabbits.
Her name was Mary Toft, from a small town called Godalming.
A local surgeon, John Howard, believed her, and spread the news.
The story reached King George the First himself. So he sent his own surgeon, Nathaniel St. André, to check.
St. André arrived just as she was said to be on rabbit number fifteen. And he believed it too.
Mary was brought to London, and curious crowds gathered outside.
Then a porter told the truth: she had tried to bribe him to sneak rabbits into her room.
A doctor threatened her with a painful operation, and she confessed. It was all a hoax.
She was jailed as a notorious and vile cheat.
Months later, she was released and went home to Godalming.
And the doctors who fell for it were mocked all over London, even by the famous artist William Hogarth.
